name: Aileen Lee
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. MIT Sloan B.S. 1992 (~22), then Morgan Stanley analyst; HBS MBA 1997 (~27); joined Kleiner Perkins in 1999 (~29); founded Cowboy Ventures and coined 'unicorn' in 2012–2013 (~42–43).
early_history_summary: Raised in Millburn, New Jersey by Chinese immigrant parents; graduated Millburn High School as senior class president, earned an MIT Sloan B.S. (1992), worked at Morgan Stanley, then completed an HBS MBA (1997) before entering venture capital at Kleiner Perkins in 1999.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Chinese immigrants; raised in Millburn, New Jersey. Father referenced as Dr. Alan Lee in local reporting; family financial detail otherwise limited in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as venture/startup domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Lee's career milestones with independent notability (KPCB partner work, Cowboy Ventures founding, coining 'unicorn') all occurred after age 26. Pre-26 record is strong education (MIT, HBS path) and early finance work, not a dated material founder/operator breakout.

name: Katrina Lake
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Stanford B.A. 2005 (~22); worked at Parthenon Group and Polyvore; founded Stitch Fix in 2011 at age 28 while finishing Harvard MBA; IPO as CEO in 2017 at age 34.
early_history_summary: Born in San Francisco; mother a Japanese immigrant public-school teacher and father a transplant hepatologist/professor. Attended Lowell High School, Stanford (2005), then consulting and Polyvore before HBS and founding Stitch Fix.
family_context_summary: Father a transplant hepatologist and professor (UCSF/University of Minnesota); mother a Japanese immigrant who taught in public schools.
parent_family_domain_summary: Professional/academic household; not a retail/fashion entrepreneurship domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Stitch Fix founding (2011) and IPO (2017) are post-26. Pre-26 path is elite education and early career roles without a dated material founder milestone at or before age 26.

name: Anne Wojcicki
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Yale biology B.S. 1996 (~23); healthcare investment analyst roles thereafter; co-founded 23andMe in 2006 at age 32–33.
early_history_summary: Youngest of three sisters raised on Stanford's campus; father Stanley Wojcicki a Stanford physics professor, mother Esther an educator/journalist. Yale biology graduate who worked as a healthcare analyst before founding 23andMe.
family_context_summary: Father Stanford physics professor emeritus; mother Esther Wojcicki educator/journalist; sisters include former YouTube CEO Susan Wojcicki.
parent_family_domain_summary: Strong academic STEM and education household in Palo Alto/Stanford ecosystem.
evidence_summary: Despite an exceptionally advantaged upbringing, her defining company 23andMe was founded in 2006 well after age 26. No independently dated material founder/operator milestone at or before 26 was identified.

name: Leah Culver
milestone_by_age_26: In June 2007, co-founded microblogging/social network Pownce with Digg cofounder Kevin Rose and Daniel Burka, serving as cofounder and lead developer; the product became a high-profile Web 2.0 peer of Twitter and was acquired by Six Apart in late 2008.
early_history_summary: From Minnesota; switched from art to computer science at the University of Minnesota (B.S. 2006). After early roles at iLoop Mobile and Instructables, she programmed Pownce largely herself and launched it with Rose and Burka in 2007 at about age 24, earning Fast Company/MIT Technology Review recognition while still under 26.
secondary_engine: Elite ecosystem network (Kevin Rose / Digg circle)
family_context_summary: From Minnesota; family financial/background details not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kevin Rose cofounder, Web 2.0 SF ecosystem, solo technical lead, Pownce acquisition
evidence_summary: Culver's ≤26 milestone is cofounding and building Pownce (2007) as lead engineer with Digg's Kevin Rose and Daniel Burka—material, dated, and multi-sourced. She had just finished a CS degree (2006) and early SF startup jobs. Fast Company (Nov 2008) identified her as a 25-year-old founder/lead developer, and MIT Technology Review featured Pownce among startups to watch with her on the cover path. Advantage stack centers on complementary high-status cofounders and scarce full-stack product engineering rather than family capital.
starting_point: Raised in Minnesota; family class/occupation not documented in reviewed sources; studied art then computer science at the University of Minnesota.
current_position: Software engineer and angel investor; former Breaker CTO (team joined Twitter/Spaces), later roles include Airbnb iOS engineering; known SF founder/engineer.

trajectory.event: Earned a B.S. in computer science from the University of Minnesota after switching from art; worked at early startups including Instructables.
Co-founded Pownce as cofounder and sole lead developer with Kevin Rose and Daniel Burka.
Pownce acquired by Six Apart; named among Fast Company's Most Influential Women in Web 2.0 and featured via MIT Technology Review startup coverage.
Co-founded Y Combinator-backed group chat startup Convore (later Grove).
Co-founded podcast app Breaker as CTO with Erik Berlin.
Breaker team joined Twitter to help build Twitter Spaces.

name: Caterina Fake
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Vassar English B.A. 1991 (~22); Netscape community forums role ~1997 (~28); co-founded Ludicorp 2002 (~33) and Flickr 2004 (~35).
early_history_summary: Born in Pittsburgh; raised in northern New Jersey by American father and Filipina mother; Choate and Vassar (English 1991). Taught herself web development in San Francisco, later co-founded Flickr with Stewart Butterfield.
family_context_summary: Raised in New Jersey by American father and Filipina mother; limited TV; arts-oriented childhood hobbies.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech/startup domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Flickr and Ludicorp founding occurred in her mid-30s. By age 26 she had elite education but no dated material product/company milestone meeting the age-26 bar.

name: Mitchell Hashimoto
milestone_by_age_26: Created and open-sourced Vagrant (first public release ~2010), which became a widely adopted tool for portable developer environments and made him well known in DevOps by about age 22–23; founded HashiCorp in mid-2012 at about age 24 to commercialize infrastructure automation tools.
early_history_summary: Started programming around age 12 (game cheats/automation) and ran a small automation business as a teen. Studied computer science at University of Washington, met Armon Dadgar on a cloud research project, released Vagrant while early in his career, then left Kiip to found HashiCorp in 2012.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources beyond early self-taught programming narrative.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen programming, Vagrant open source, UW peer Armon Dadgar, DevOps wave
evidence_summary: Multiple sources date Vagrant's creation/popularity to ~2010 when Hashimoto was about 22 and HashiCorp's founding to 2012 at about 24—both well under 26. Business Insider (2014) described him as a 25-year-old HashiCorp CEO whose Vagrant work made him famous by 23. Leverage came from deep self-directed systems work, open-source distribution, and a durable cofounder partnership rather than inherited capital.
starting_point: Not fully documented; began serious self-taught programming around age 12 and early teen automation side projects before University of Washington CS.
current_position: Independent developer (Ghostty terminal emulator); former HashiCorp cofounder/CEO/CTO who left before/around the company's IPO era; HashiCorp later acquired by IBM (2025).

trajectory.event: Released Vagrant, an open-source tool for portable, reproducible developer environments that rapidly gained DevOps adoption.
Founded HashiCorp to build a commercial company around infrastructure automation open-source tools.
Armon Dadgar joined as cofounder; company expanded beyond Vagrant into a multi-product suite.
Raised significant venture capital (reported ~$10M) as a young CEO while Vagrant ecosystem tools proliferated.
HashiCorp IPO; Hashimoto had already stepped back from day-to-day CEO leadership earlier.
Left HashiCorp and focused on independent engineering projects including Ghostty.
IBM completed acquisition of HashiCorp; Hashimoto continued independent product work.

name: Armon Dadgar
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Mitchell Hashimoto as cofounder of HashiCorp in July 2013 (about age 24), helping build the open-source infrastructure automation company that later produced Consul, Terraform, Vault, and related products and became a major DevOps vendor.
early_history_summary: Met Hashimoto at University of Washington around 2008 on a research project exposing academic users to early public-cloud tech. Graduated UW CS (B.S. 2011), worked as a software engineer (including at Kiip), then moved to San Francisco and cofounded HashiCorp in 2013 as CTO.
family_context_summary: Sources note Brooklyn birth in some profiles; family financial/domain details not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: UW research peer Mitchell Hashimoto, early cloud systems work, HashiCorp cofounder/CTO
evidence_summary: Dadgar's age-26-eligible milestone is cofounding HashiCorp in 2013 at about age 24, corroborated by HashiCorp's origin story and multiple profiles (including contemporaneous notes that he was 24 while Hashimoto was 26 when seeking professional management help). Prior UW CS and systems research plus Kiip engineering provided relevant reps; advantage is primarily peer cofounder leverage and scarce distributed-systems skill on a cloud-automation wave.
starting_point: Not fully documented; University of Washington CS path with early research exposure to public cloud technologies around 2008–2010.
current_position: Former longtime HashiCorp cofounder and CTO; stepped down after ~13 years around the IBM acquisition period (2025–2026 reporting).

trajectory.event: Graduated University of Washington with a B.S. in computer science after research work on cloud systems.
Joined Mitchell Hashimoto as cofounder/CTO of HashiCorp in San Francisco.
HashiCorp raised institutional venture funding while shipping additional open-source infrastructure tools.
Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 for transforming enterprise technology.
HashiCorp completed its IPO while Dadgar remained technical cofounder/CTO.
HashiCorp joined IBM following acquisition; Dadgar later stepped down after nearly 13 years.

name: Solomon Hykes
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Paris-based platform-as-a-service company dotCloud in 2008 (about age 25) with Kamel Founadi and Sebastien Pahl; the company later pivoted and rebranded around the Docker container project that transformed software packaging and deployment.
early_history_summary: Born in New York City to an American father and French-Canadian mother; moved to France at about age four. Studied computer science at Epitech in Paris and started coding young. Founded dotCloud in 2008, entered Y Combinator in 2010, and open-sourced Docker in 2013 after pivoting the company.
family_context_summary: Born in NYC; American father and French-Canadian mother; raised largely in France after age four.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech domain expertise in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Epitech, early PaaS founding, YC later, Docker pivot
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Docker corporate history date the company founding as dotCloud in 2008 in Paris—Hykes's age ~25. That founding is the ≤26 material milestone; Docker's mass adoption and unicorn status came later (2013+). Early advantage is technical product insight and cofounder execution more than inherited capital or elite U.S. VC networks at the first founding.
starting_point: Born in New York City; raised in France after early childhood; studied computer science at Epitech in Paris.
current_position: Founder of Dagger (programmable CI/CD); former Docker cofounder/CEO/CTO who left Docker in 2018.

trajectory.event: Co-founded dotCloud in Paris as a platform-as-a-service company.
Joined an early Y Combinator batch and incorporated/expanded the company in the U.S.
Open-sourced Docker and pivoted the company from PaaS to containers; company later renamed Docker, Inc.
Docker reached unicorn-scale private valuation after major fundraising.
Stepped down from Docker after roughly a decade building the company.
Founded Dagger, a container-native programmable CI/CD engine.

name: Eric Yuan
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Chinese university degrees in applied math/CS and geology engineering; married young while a master's student; moved to Silicon Valley in 1997 at age 27 to join early WebEx; founded Zoom in 2011 at age 41.
early_history_summary: Son of geological engineers in Tai'an, Shandong; earned degrees in China and was inspired by videotelephony during long train visits to his girlfriend. After Japan training and multiple U.S. visa attempts, joined WebEx as an early engineer in 1997, later becoming a Cisco VP after acquisition, then founding Zoom.
family_context_summary: Parents were geological engineers; childhood included resourcefulness such as collecting scraps for copper cash in grade school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents in geological engineering—technical household but not videoconferencing/software entrepreneurship.
evidence_summary: Yuan's first U.S. tech role (WebEx, 1997) began at age 27; Zoom founding was at 41. No specific dated material milestone at or before age 26 was identified despite later legendary success.

name: Brian Halligan
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. UVM electrical engineering B.S. 1990 (~23); sales leadership at PTC and Groove Networks in his 30s; MIT Sloan MBA 2005 (~38); co-founded HubSpot in June 2006 at age ~39.
early_history_summary: Born/raised in Westwood, Massachusetts; UVM EE 1990; long enterprise software sales career (PTC, Groove Networks) before MIT Sloan MBA and cofounding HubSpot with Dharmesh Shah.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Westwood, Massachusetts public schools; family occupation details not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: HubSpot founding and inbound-marketing fame arrived in his late 30s. By 26 he had a UVM degree and early career start but no dated material founder/product milestone meeting the bar.

name: Cheng Wei
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Beijing University of Chemical Technology graduate; Alibaba/Alipay sales career from ~2005; founded Didi Dache / Beijing Xiaoju Technology in 2012 at age 29.
early_history_summary: Born May 19, 1983 in Shangrao, Jiangxi; ordinary family background per Chinese profiles. After university, worked sales roles including at Alibaba Group before resigning in 2012 to found the taxi-hailing app that became DiDi.
family_context_summary: Born into an ordinary family in Yanshan County, Shangrao, Jiangxi Province per Chinese biographical sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech/transport domain expertise.
evidence_summary: DiDi founding in 2012 at age 29 is the breakout. Pre-26 record is university plus early sales career at Alibaba—not a material independently famous founder milestone by 26.

name: Zhang Yiming
milestone_by_age_26: In 2009, at age 26, founded 99fang.com by taking over Kuxun's real-estate search business as Expedia prepared to acquire Kuxun's travel unit—his first company as founder/CEO—after earlier roles as Kuxun's first engineer (2006) and brief stints at Microsoft and Fanfou.
early_history_summary: Born April 1, 1983 in Longyan, Fujian to civil-servant parents; only son. Nankai University computer engineering BEng 2005. Joined travel search startup Kuxun as fifth employee/first engineer in 2006, rose to technical director, briefly worked at Microsoft and Fanfou, then founded 99fang in 2009 before starting ByteDance in 2012.
secondary_engine: Scarce technical depth + early startup reps
family_context_summary: Only son of civil servants in Longyan, Fujian; not a wealthy tech dynasty background per Bloomberg/Wikipedia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were civil servants; no documented tech entrepreneurship domain transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kuxun first engineer, 99fang founder, China mobile internet wave
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and multiple profiles document founding 99fang.com in 2009 at age 26 after deep early-operator reps as Kuxun's first engineer from age 22. That first founding is a dated material milestone within the age-26 bar; ByteDance (2012) at 29 is the later legendary breakout. Early advantage is accumulated product/engineering judgment in Chinese consumer internet rather than family capital or elite Western pipelines.
starting_point: Born in Longyan, Fujian to civil-servant parents as an only son; studied microelectronics then software/computer engineering at Nankai University (graduated 2005).
current_position: ByteDance founder and major controlling shareholder (reported >50% voting rights); stepped down as CEO in 2021; among the world's richest people with estimated tens of billions net worth; resides largely outside day-to-day ops (Singapore associations reported).

trajectory.event: Joined travel search startup Kuxun as fifth employee and first engineer; later became technical director.
Founded 99fang.com, spinning out Kuxun's real-estate search business as his first company.
Co-founded ByteDance with Liang Rubo and launched Toutiao, an AI-driven news aggregator.
Launched Douyin (TikTok internationally), which became a global short-video platform.
Stepped down as ByteDance CEO after announcing a leadership handover while retaining major voting control.
Reported as China's richest person at points amid TikTok/ByteDance valuation surges.
